note: Fits the starting-point half of the ICP almost perfectly and fails the commercial half outright. He is exactly the good-to-great case the definition describes: 170lb at 5'9", trains already, owns kettlebells, holds a gym membership, and wants a recomposition of 10 to 15lb and to look like someone who works out — not rescue, and about as far from gym-averse as the corpus gets. Health is plainly the neglected corner of a functioning life. But he is a salaried office worker who has moved back in with his parents at 30, not a business owner, physician or equivalent, and the income criterion fails without ambiguity: 'I don't got 6,000 bucks laying around' and 'from a financial standpoint, that will be an issue.' The instructive part is that this is the reverse of the usual failure mode in this batch — most prospects here miss on starting point and pass on money; he is the one who genuinely wants what the programme sells and simply cannot pay for it.
